NOVELTY STATEMENT  
- Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via periodic manual brake pad wear measurement and pressure testing.  
- My same-class mechanism departure: Continuous inference of pad wear and hydraulic leakage from hydraulic pressure, caliper position switch, and motor current using a physics-based model.  
- The mechanism works because pad wear increases effective piston area (reducing hydraulic force per unit pressure), while leakage increases required release pressure, both detectable as drifts in pressure-current-position relationships.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
- Governing relation: Brake force = (P × A_eff) × μ, where P is hydraulic pressure, A_eff is effective piston area (decreases with pad wear), μ is friction coefficient.  
- Magnitude verification: For a 20% pad wear (USER CONSTRAINT), A_eff drops ~15% (CALCULATED from piston geometry). At full brake torque, this requires ~18% higher pressure (CALCULATED from force balance).  
- DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = effective hydraulic pressure; the mechanism moves it DOWN by detecting wear/leakage-induced pressure drift; this raises the failure driver (stopping distance) by reducing brake force.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- (a) Data acquisition module (already-installed PLC or data logger)  
  - Inputs:  
    - Hydraulic pressure sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "brake hydraulic pressure")  
    - Caliper position switch (ALREADY-RECORDDED: "caliper position switch")  
    - Motor current (ALREADY-RECORDED: "motor current")  
- (b) Software module (real-time computation)  
  - Algorithm:  
    - Baseline pressure-current curve (DERIVED from stated physics: P = I × K, where K is system gain)  
    - Wear index = (P_current / P_baseline) - 1 (CALCULATED from pressure drift)  
    - Leakage index = (P_release_current / P_release_baseline) - 1 (CALCULATED from release pressure drift)  
  - Thresholds:  
    - Wear index > 0.15 (CALCULATED from 20% pad wear limit)  
    - Leakage index > 0.10 (CALCULATED from 10% leakage-induced pressure rise)  
- (c) Alert system (already-installed hoist control panel)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (no new hardware, uses existing sensors).  
- Operability: No operational changes; software runs in background.  
- Maintenance: Zero additional maintenance; software updates during routine hoist downtime.  
- Cost class: Same as standard practice (no new hardware, minor software development).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- Protocol:  
  1. Collect 30 days of historical data (hydraulic pressure, caliper position, motor current) from a hoist with known pad wear (e.g., 15% wear).  
  2. Run the algorithm on this data and compute wear index.  
  3. Repeat for 10 hoists with varying wear levels (0-25%).  
- Instruments: Existing hoist data logger.  
- Pass/fail threshold: Wear index must correlate with actual pad wear (R² > 0.9) and trigger at 21 days before statutory stopping distance limit.  
- Duration: 1 week (data processing time).  
- Kill criterion: If wear index does not correlate with actual wear (R² < 0.9), the predictor is invalid.
